title: Typical tactics and plans
intro:
# Typical tactics and plans

Eight positions, each one running through a line from an earlier chapter and stopping on the move that matters. Play the line and find the last move yourself.

## What each one is about

The first is the storm. The centre is closed, the f-pawn has gone to f4 and the g-pawn to g5, and the piece that decides the attack is the rook: it lifts to f6 and h6, and the queen comes to h5 behind it while White is taking a pawn on the other wing.

The second is the knight on f4. It got there by way of h5 because the knight on f3 was in the bishop's way, and when White plays g3 to push it, the pawn on h3 is the one it takes.

The third and fourth are the ...Nxe4 trick, twice: once after the queens have come off in the Classical, where a knight on d5 looks like a fork and is not one, and once in the h3 line, where White takes a pawn on e5 that the knight on f6 was only pretending to hold. In chapter 1 the same capture loses the exchange when White has not castled, so the third exercise is also about counting.

The fifth is the ...Qb6 trick: a knight on g4 that cannot be taken because the queen behind it hits d4 and b2 both, and the queen that lands on d4 afterwards has to be brought home without walking into the pawn on e4.

The sixth is the exchange of the dark bishop. The bishop on g7 is the defence and is never traded for nothing; here it goes to h6 to hit the knight on d2, and when the bishop on c1 has nowhere to go the trade is right, because the f-pawn goes next.

The seventh and eighth are defence against the queenside pawns. In the Petrosian, b4 arrives with the rook behind it and the answer is ...axb4 and a knight to a4, where taking it hands Black a bishop that looks at d1 and turns White's c5 break into a lost queen. In the other, White pushes b4 with a knight on c5 in the way, and the a-pawn takes because the pawn on b6 is holding the knight.

## Typical mistakes at this level

Lifting the rook before the f-pawn has closed the kingside. Retreating the knight from f4 when it can take on h3. Playing ...Nxe4 with the king still on e1 for White, when Nxc7 forks the rooks. Trading the bishop on g7 because a trade is available rather than because the c1 bishop is stuck. And answering b4 by retreating the knight, when the a-pawn takes and the knight goes forward.

tree.note: The bishop to e2, and it is chapter 1.

children.note: The knight to a6, chapter 1's move.
The rook steps off the pin.
The knight jumps in, and it looks like a fork.

Exercise 3: take on e4. The fork on e7 wins nothing, because the knight on e7 is traded for the bishop on c8 and the pawn on e4 was free. The same capture loses when White has not castled, because Nxc7 hits both rooks; here the rook on a8 is covered by the knight on a6.

mistakes.note: 12.Nc3 and the ending is level, with the pawn on e4 still on the board: the capture on e4 is the exercise.
12.cxd5 Nb8 13.Rac1 and the pawn on d5 is a wedge with the bishop pair White's and the knight back on b8.

children.note: The bishop steps back, and the pawn is gone for nothing.
Exercise 3, the last move: the knight to b4, hitting a2 and c2 and the square d3. The extra pawn is on the board and every Black piece has a job.

mistakes.note: Sound and the same count: 15.g3 Nb4 and the knight comes a move later.
Sound: 15.Rad1 Nb4 and the same.
Sound: 15.Bxc5+ Nxc5 and the knights have been traded on White's terms; the knight to b4 keeps both.

children.plan: ...Nxa2 or ...Nc2 when it is free, ...f5 to hold the knight on e4, ...Ke7 and the rooks to the d-file. A pawn up with the better minor pieces.
children.name: Exercise 3: the ...Nxe4 trick, castled

children.note: The pawn asks the knight to leave.
Exercise 5: the queen to b6. The knight on g4 cannot be taken yet, because the queen hits d4 and b2 both, and White has to answer the threat first.

mistakes.note: 12.Nf3 and the knight has gone back with nothing to show for the trip.
Sound: 12.Nf3 Nxf3+ 13.Qxf3 and White has the bishop pair. The queen move keeps the pawn.

children.note: The queen holds e4 and g4.
The pawn to g3, taking f4 from the queen and preparing Bf4.
The knight to c5, hitting e4 a second time. Bf4 is coming to hit the queen, and the knight is placed first so that the queen has e7 to go to with the knight covering d3 and e4.

mistakes.note: Sound: 15.Bf4 Be5 and the queen has left e5 for the bishop. The knight first hits e4.
15.Qxe4 and the queen has gone for a pawn: e4 was held by the queen, the rook and the knight.

children.note: Exercise 5, the last move: the queen to e7, home and safe. Not e8, where Bxd6 forks the queen and the knight, and not f6, where the queen is hit by Bxd6 and Nd4 both. The knight on c5 holds e4 and d3, and Black has a pawn for nothing with the queens likely to stay on.

mistakes.note: 16.Bxd6 and the bishop forks the queen and the knight on c5: the queen on e8 was the one square that lost a piece.
16.Rad1 Ne6 17.Bxd6 and the pawn on d6 has gone with the queen on f6 hit next by Nd4.
16.Rad1 Be5 17.Qe3 and the queen on e6 is in the way of the bishop on c8.

children.plan: ...Be5 to trade the bishop on f4, ...Re8 and ...Bd7, ...Nxe4 when it is free. A pawn up with the kingside pawns on g4 and g3 loose.
children.name: Exercise 5: the ...Qb6 trick

children.note: Hold the knight with the pawn.
The knight to b3, to trade the knight on c5.
Exercise 8: the knight to d7, holding c5 a second time so that Nxc5 is met by a knight and not a pawn, and stepping aside for the f-pawn. Two jobs in one move.

mistakes.note: 14.Qxb3 and the queen is on b3 hitting b7 with the f-pawn still at home: the knight was worth keeping.
Sound: 14.Rae1 Bd7 and the knight has stepped back. The knight to d7 holds c5 and prepares ...f5 both.
14.Bd2 and the knight on g4 has nothing to do with h3 coming.

children.note: Take back with the knight, so that the pawn on b6 still holds it and the structure is untouched.

mistakes.note: 15.Nb5 and the knight is in with the pawn on a5 loose: the structure has been given away.
15.Rad1 and the pawn on d6 has gone from the centre with the d-file White's.

children.note: The storm: the pawn to b4, hitting the knight on c5 with the a-pawn behind it.

Exercise 8, the last move: the a-pawn takes. The knight on c5 is held by the pawn on b6, so b4 threatened nothing it could carry out, and the pawn on b4 is now Black's with the a-file open behind it. The knight on c3 has to move and the queenside is Black's.

mistakes.note: 16.bxa5 and the pawn has gone with the knight on the rim.
16.Nb5 and the knight is in on b5 with c5 coming: the knight on c5 left the square that was holding everything.
16.a3 and the knight on b7 is out of the game with the storm a move on.

children.plan: ...Qe7 and ...f5, ...Ra3 when the knight on c3 has moved, ...Bd7 and ...Rfb8. The storm hit a knight that was held, and the pawn it pushed is Black's.
children.name: Exercise 8: the storm meets the a-pawn

children.note: The bishop to h6, hitting the knight on d2.
The queen holds the knight, and the bishop on c1 is pinned to the job of holding d2.
Exercise 6: the knight to e8. It steps aside for the f-pawn and covers d6, and the bishop on h6 stays: White cannot play Bb2 without losing d2, so the bishop on c1 has to sit.

mistakes.note: 12.Bxd2 and the bishop on g7 has been traded for a knight, which is the one trade the setup never makes without a reason: the reason was coming, and it was the bishop on c1.
12.Bxh5 gxh5 13.Nf3 and the kingside is broken.
Sound: 12.Bb2 Rg8 and the g-file is Black's. The knight to e8 keeps ...f5 as the plan.

children.note: The knight moves out of the pin.
Take the bishop. The knight has left d2, so the bishop on h6 has nothing to hit there, and the bishop on c1 is the one White wanted on b2: it goes, and the f-pawn goes next.

mistakes.note: 13.Bb2 and the bishop has gone back to g7 with White's bishop on b2 where it wanted to be: the trade was there and was not taken.
13.Bxh6 fxe4 14.Ng5 and the bishop on g7 has gone for nothing with the knight arriving on g5: the trade on c1 first.

children.note: Exercise 6, the last move: the break. With the dark bishops off, White's king has no bishop to hold the dark squares, and the pawn on f5 opens the f-file for the rook that is already there.

mistakes.note: Sound: 14.a3 f5 and the same a move later.
Sound: 14.a3 f5 and the same. The break first.
14.a3 and the break has been delayed with the bishop on d7 doing nothing.

children.plan: ...Nf6 and ...Qe7, ...fxe4 when Nxe4 lets the knight on c5 trade, ...Rf7 and ...Raf8. The dark squares around White's king are Black's.
children.name: Exercise 6: the ...Bh6 exchange

children.note: White closes the centre at once.
The pawn to a5, and chapter 1's Petrosian answer.
The knight to e1, for f3 and Nd3.
The knight steps aside for the f-pawn.
The rook to b1 for b4: the race is on, and White's is the slower one.
Exercise 1: the rook lifts. With the kingside closed, the rook goes to f6 and h6 in front of the king it is attacking, and the queen comes to h5 behind it. Nothing on the queenside matters yet.

mistakes.note: Sound: 14.a3 g4 and the knight is going to h5. The rook lift is the faster attack.
Sound: 14.b3 b6 and the knight is held. The rook first, because the queenside is White's and the kingside is Black's.
14.a3 and a move has been spent on the wing where White is attacking.
14.fxg4 and the f-file has opened for White's rook with the pawn on f4 loose.

children.note: The queen hits a5 and the knight on d7.
The queen to e8, holding d7 and going to h5. The pawn on a5 is given up for the tempo.

mistakes.note: 15.Qxd7 and the knight has gone: the queen on a4 was hitting it.
15.Qxa5 and the pawn has gone with the knight on b6 in the way of the b-pawn it was meant to hold.

children.note: The queen takes the pawn, and it is a long way from the kingside.
The queen to h5, behind the rook. ...Rh6 next and the pawn on h2 is hit twice with the g-pawn ready to go to g4.

mistakes.note: Sound and the same attack in the other order: 16.g4 fxg3 17.Bxg3 Nf6 and the queen comes to h5 next. The queen first, because it is the piece White cannot answer.
16.Nd3 and the bishop has gone back with the attack a move slower.
16.c5 and the rook on g6 is not the lift: h6 is the square, with h2 the target.

children.note: The king steps to the corner.
Exercise 1, the last move: the rook to h6. The pawn on h2 is hit by the rook and the queen, Bg1 is the only defence, and ...Nf6 with ...g4 comes next. White's queen is on a5.

mistakes.note: 17.Bg1 and the knight on b6 has left the kingside, where the attack is.
17.fxg4 Qg5 18.b4 and the pawn has gone with the f-file open for White's rook: the rook lift first.
The pawn on h2 is held by the king: 17.Kxh2 and the queen has gone.

children.plan: ...Nf6 and ...g4, ...Nh5 to g3 when the bishop has gone to g1. The queenside pawn White took is worth nothing against the kingside it left.
children.name: Exercise 1: the storm and the rook lift

children.note: The Petrosian: the pin with the pawn on d5.
The knight steps aside for the f-pawn.
The storm begins: a3, b3 and b4 with the rook coming to b1.
Exercise 7 begins: the pawn to h5. The bishop on h4 has g3 taken from it by the pawn on f4 that will come, and the bishop on g7 is going to h6 next to hit the knight on d2.

mistakes.note: Sound: 13.b3 h5 and the same a move later. The pawn first, so that ...Bh6 comes with the pawn on h5 holding g4.
13.exf5 Bxf5 14.f3 and the centre has opened with the knight on a6 out of things.
13.f3 h5 14.Rb1 and a move has been spent on the wing where White is attacking.

children.note: The pawn holds e4 and takes g4 from the knight.
The bishop out, and the queen's rook is connected for the a-file.

mistakes.note: Sound: 14.Kh1 Bd7 and the same. The bishop on c8 first, so that ...Na4 later comes with the bishop taking back.
14.b4 axb4 15.axb4 Na4 16.Nxa4 and the knight has been traded before the bishop on c8 could take back: the bishop first.

children.note: The pawn to b3, for b4.
The bishop to h6, hitting the knight on d2 and pinning it to the bishop on c1 behind it.

mistakes.note: Sound: 15.Rb1 Bh6 and the same a move later. The bishop first, because the knight on d2 has to be held before b4.
15.exf5 gxf5 16.Bd3 and the kingside has opened with the bishop on h4 looking at e7.

children.note: The rook to b1, and b4 is next.
The knight to c5, hitting e4 and standing on the square b4 is about to hit: the answer to b4 is prepared, and it is ...axb4 and ...Na4.

mistakes.note: Sound and the engine's choice: 16.Bf2 Qe7 and the bishop has traded the pin for the diagonal. The knight to c5 keeps the exercise's idea.
Sound: 16.Kh1 Nc5 and the same a move later.

children.note: Take, so that the a-file is open and the knight has a4.

mistakes.note: 17.Nxa4 Bxa4 18.bxa5 and the pawn on a5 has gone with the a-file White's.
17.Nxb3 and the knight has gone: b3 was covered by the knight on d2.

children.note: The pawn takes back, hitting the knight.

Exercise 7, the last move: the knight to a4. It cannot be taken for nothing, because the bishop on d7 takes back and then hits d1 through the pawn on b3 that has gone; and if White then breaks with c5, the bishop takes the queen. The storm has been met on the square it was aimed at.

mistakes.note: 18.Kh1 and the knight is on the rim with the pawn on b4 fixed and c5 coming.
18.fxe4 and the knight has gone for a pawn: e4 was held by the pawn on f3.
Sound: 18.Bf2 Bxf2+ 19.Rxf2 Na4 and the same knight a move later. The knight first keeps the bishop.

children.plan: ...Bxa4 after Nxa4, ...f5 with the queen on e8 behind it, and ...Ra3 for the a-file. If 18.Nxa4 Bxa4 19.c5 then 19...Bxd1 takes the queen, because the bishop on a4 sees d1 with the pawn on b3 gone. White's storm has left the queenside open and Black's king has nothing to fear.
children.name: Exercise 7: the storm met by ...Na4

tree.note: The pawn to h3, chapter 4's line.

children.note: The knight to h5, with the knight on f3 in the bishop's way.
The pawn asks the knight to leave f4.
Exercise 2: take on h3. The knight cannot be taken back, because the bishop on f1 has gone to f3 and the knight on h2 does not see h3. A pawn up with the king's cover gone, and ...f4 next.

mistakes.note: 13.Nxe4 and the knight on f4 has to decide with the centre opened on White's terms and the knight on e4 the best piece on the board. The capture on h3 wins a pawn first.
13.gxf4 exf4 14.Bd2 and the knight has gone for two pawns with the position closed.
13.Bxh5 gxh5 14.exf5 and the kingside is broken with a pawn gone and the knight back where it came from.

children.note: The queen holds the bishop and looks at h6.
Exercise 2, the last move: the pawn to f4. The bishop on e3 is hit, and after gxf4 exf4 the knight on h3 and the bishop on g7 both see the dark squares White has just given up.

mistakes.note: 14.Bxc5 dxc5 15.Bg2 and the knight on h3 is hit by the bishop with nothing holding it.
14.Nxe4 Nc5 15.Bxc5 dxc5 16.Qh6 and the knight on h3 is loose with the queen arriving: the push keeps the knight held.

children.note: Take back, and the bishop on e3 is hit with the bishop on g7 looking at b2 and the knight on h3 a pawn up.

mistakes.note: 15.Bxf4 exf4 16.Qxf4 and the pawn count is level again.

children.plan: ...Nc5 and ...Bd7, ...Qe5 with the bishop on g7 behind it, ...Rf7 and ...Raf8. A pawn up with White's king open.
children.name: Exercise 2: the knight on f4 takes on h3

children.note: Exercise 2, the other way: the pawn to e4. The bishop on f3 is hit with the knight on f4 behind the push, and the pawn on f5 is not going anywhere.

mistakes.note: Sound: 13.O-O Ng6 14.Bh5 and the pawns are level. The push wins more.
Sound: 13.O-O Nc5 and the pawn is back. The push wins more.
13.O-O Bxf5 14.Bxc5 dxc5 15.Ne4 and the pawn is back with White's knight on e4.

children.plan: ...Bxf5 after Nxe4, ...Nxh3 when the bishop on f3 has moved, ...Nc5 and ...Nb4. A pawn up and the initiative.
children.name: Exercise 2: the pawn to e4

children.note: Exercise 4: take on e4. The knight leaves f6 with tempo, and the bishop on g7 sees e5 now.
Take the knight. Level, with White's king on e1.
Exercise 4, the last move: the rook to d4, hitting the knight on e4 and the pawn on c4 both. The rook is not hit by anything, and the bishop on e5 holds it.

mistakes.note: Sound: the rook holds the bishop from e8, and 12.Nf6+ is answered by 12...Bxf6+ with check from the rook behind it. The rook to d4 hits the knight and the pawn on c4 instead.
12.Nxf6+ Bxf6 13.Bxf6 and the bishop on g7 has gone for the knight: the pawn on f6 walked into a fork.
Sound: 12.Bxd8 Bxa1 and the rooks have been traded for each other with the bishop on a1 to come out. The rook to d4 keeps more.

children.note: The king steps up, and the knight on f6 is hit by the bishop on e5.

mistakes.note: 13.Nd5 c6 14.Be3 and the rook on d4 is hit with the king on f8 in the way of the rook on h8: the king on g7 keeps everything connected.
13.Bxf6 and the bishop on g7 has gone for the knight: the bishop pair, which was the point of the ending, has been given away.

children.note: Push the knight. It goes back, and Black has the better bishop, the d-file and the pawn on c4 to aim at.

mistakes.note: 14.Bf6+ Kg8 15.Bxd4 and the rook has gone: the bishop on d6 stopped holding d4.
Sound: 14.Be3 Bxb2 15.Rb1 and the pawn count is level. The knight first.

children.plan: ...Nd7 and ...Nc5, ...Be6 hitting c4, ...Rd8 for the file. The pawn White took on e5 came back with interest.
children.name: Exercise 4: ...Nxe4 in the h3 line
